title: TA8-12400
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of Kazakhstan, claims refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1 The hearing was adjourned on 14 April 2010 pending counsel's written submissions that were due on 21 April 2010 and were received by the Refugee Division on 22 April.
The basis for the claim is set out in the claimant's Personal Information Form narrative (PIF).2 The following is a summary.
The claimant claims a well founded fear of persecution based on membership in a particular social group - homosexual men.

He fears the Kazakhstan people and the authorities who hate gays. He claims he experienced beatings, a death threat by the police, threatening notes and slashed tires and broken windshields because of his sexual orientation. He was allegedly attacked in XXXXX 2003, XXXXX 2007 and XXXXX 2008. He made the decision to leave Kazakhstan and in April 2008 he applied for a Canadian visitor visa. He left from XXXXX on XXXXX XXXXX 2008 and arrived in Canada the next day. He made a claim for protection on 24 June 2008.

I have given consideration to the totality of the evidence and counsel's submissions and I find that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. I find that the claimant was entirely lacking in credibility. I find that he has failed to provide sufficient credible and trustworthy evidence that he would face a reasonable chance of persecution for a Convention ground. I also considered whether on a balance of probabilities he would be personally subject to a risk to life or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if returned to Kazakhstan and determine he would not.
The determinative issue is credibility and whether he has established a well founded fear of persecution based on sexual orientation. Late Disclosure

The claimant's claim for protection was made on 24 June 2008 and on 23 July 2008 he signed his PIF. At that time he had the same legal representation as he had at the hearing. No personal documents or other disclosure was made prior to the hearing date. At the hearing a package of fifteen items was left on the Member's desk that included letters and medical reports and other personal documents in support of the claimant's claim. Counsel's only explanation for the late disclosure was that it had been sitting on his secretary's desk. Counsel acknowledged his familiarity with the twenty day disclosure rule. The documents were taken into evidence given the late disclosure was explained as being through no fault of the claimant. Identity

I find the claimant's identity as a citizen of Kazakhstan is established by the oral testimony and personal documents filed, including his passport.3 I do not find that the claimant has established his identity as a homosexual with credible and trustworthy evidence. Credibility

Credibility emerged as the key issue in this claim. The claimant contradicted his own evidence several times. There were inconsistencies between the documents, the PIF, and the oral evidence concerning the nature and seriousness of his injuries after he was beaten, and whether or not he even went to the hospital, and received treatment. The claimant acted in a contrary manner to an earlier statement he gave about gays reporting to police. There were inconsistencies about the dates and nature of the claimant's employment4 and work history between the PIF, the oral evidence and the Immigration interview forms. The claimant provided inconsistent information about his living arrangements before and after he moved to XXXXX in XXXXX 2008. The claimant provided inconsistent information as to whether his boyfriend's parents knew about their relationship. There were material omissions in the PIF. The claimant failed to amend his PIF to include a fear of being killed by Muslims. Between the evidence in the PIF and the oral testimony provided at the hearing the claimant provided two completely different scenarios relating to the same incident in XXXXX 2003. In the PIF he indicated he was not seriously injured and did not go to the hospital or report the attack to the police; at the hearing he testified to sustaining serious injuries and provided a medical report showing he went to the hospital within hours of the attack. Due to the extent and number of inconsistencies and contradicting evidence provided by the claimant and the questionable documents disclosed last minute I find there to be a pattern of fabrication that gives rise to doubts generally about the claimant's veracity.5 As a result I do not accept on a balance of probabilities that he is homosexual or that he suffered the attacks and threats he alleged. These are some examples of the evidence that gave rise to my credibility findings.

In the PIF the claimant listed his employment as a self employed XXXXX XXXXX from XXXXX 2003 to XXXXX 2008. He provided no other entry under Work Experience. In Schedule 1 he similarly listed his employment from 2003 to 2008 as a XXXXX XXXXX. At the hearing he contradicted this information and said he was not a XXXXX XXXXX and testified he was a partner in a XXXXX XXXXX business when he left XXXXX in XXXXX 2008. He could not say when he began the XXXXX XXXXX business but guessed it was in 2006. He could not remember if this was his only business in 2006, but said it was in 2007 and 2008. There is nothing in the PIF or the employment history provided to Immigration6 to indicate he ever had a partnership in XXXXX XXXXX. When confronted with the information in the PIF about being a self-employed XXXXX XXXXX he then described his work as a XXXXX for his brother in law's business. He could not provide a date when he began or ended this work. The claimant had no explanation for not mentioning the XXXXX XXXXX business in the PIF or Immigration forms. I make an adverse finding of the claimant's credibility based on the inconsistent information he gave about his employment and his unwillingness to provide any explanation or motivation for attempting to mislead about what he was doing in Kazakhstan for several years prior to leaving.

The claimant was aware that he could amend his PIF. His counsel indicated at the outset two errors the claimant had brought to his attention and these amendments were made before the PIF was filed as a sworn exhibit. The first change was at line one of the narrative to change the name of the city where he was born to XXXXX from XXXXX. The second change, on page six of the narrative, was that "three" men and not two, strangled a hairdresser. No other amendments or additions were made to the claimant's PIF. The claimant did not make an addition to his PIF to include evidence to which he would later testify about concerning his fear of being killed by an organization called "League of Muslims - Shahids".7 At the hearing he testified to fearing them after reading an article he disclosed in Exhibit C-2 that had come to his attention several months earlier through the internet. This fear of Muslims was brought out by the claimant only in response to the Tribunal Officer's question about whether the claimant would be able in 2010 to live safely in XXXXX. The claimant said the reason he could not live in XXXXX was due to the Muslims agenda to kill all of the gays. Prior to this statement the claimant omitted any specific fear of Muslims at his Immigration interview, in his PIF or in his previous oral testimony. He had not indicated in his PIF any fear of persecution based on religion. The claimant failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the omission about Muslims. He said he learned about it after he spoke with his counsel about six months ago but did not explain why he did not add this fear prior to the hearing or filing the PIF as an exhibit. He claims the Muslims believe being gay is a sin and they don't deserve to live. When asked about the disclosed XXXXX 2009 article in Exhibit C-2 he had little information and did not even know whether or not the Muslims had taken any action against the gays in XXXXX or elsewhere. He was not aware of any additional documents relating to this agenda. I find such an omission to be serious. I draw an adverse credibility finding and reject as unsatisfactory his explanation for the omission was because he read the article after he signed the PIF.

The claimant provided inconsistent information about an alleged attack on him on XXXXX XXXXX 2008 when he was pushed down stairs and beaten by three unknown attackers. In the PIF, signed in July 2008 months after the alleged attack he stated "fortunately my injuries were not too serious being only bruising and pain all over my body I did not go to the hospital believing that the police would have been called and that would be too dangerous". At the hearing, more than two years after the attack, his evidence is he went to a clinic and the diagnosis was serious. He said he suffered a concussion when he fell down the stairs and within hours of the attack he went to the hospital for treatment and needed an ultrasound. The claimant also disclosed a medical record8 dated XXXXX XXXXX with a diagnosis that included moderate brain concussion, multiple face and back scratches, bruises on the back. In the report it was recommended that the claimant consult a "neurosurgeon, traumatologist and urologist" which he said he did not do. The claimant provided no explanation for these major inconsistencies between his evidence in his PIF and his oral evidence. He said "I don't know must have been a mistake in translation". I reject this explanation as unsatisfactory. I find the description of injuries in the medical report that was disclosed at the hearing to be in such stark contrast to evidence provided eighteen months earlier, which was never amended that I reject the medical report and the evidence regarding this attack in XXXXX 2008 as not credible. I find the evidence to be so inconsistent that in the absence of an explanation as to why this is the case I find the incident never took place. I draw an adverse credibility finding concerning the claimant in that he provided contradictory and inconsistent evidence and suspect documentary evidence that is believed to have been manufactured for the purpose of embellishing a claim for protection and for no other reason.

The claimant stated in the PIF that he and a boyfriend were beaten up in XXXXX 2003. He described being punched by five men, and cut with a knife. He wrote that he did not go to the hospital because the cut was not serious and he did not go to the police out of fear it would do more harm than good.

Notwithstanding his concerns about the police in 2003 the claimant claims in XXXXX 2007, the one and only time he called the police, he detailed the intimate behaviour he and his boyfriend were engaged in prior to the attack. He told the officer they were holding hands, hugging and kissing. The police response to this was to call them abnormal and threaten to shoot them if they saw them again. The claimant said after that "we just went home". The claimant wrote nothing in the PIF about being injured or going to the hospital after the police left.

At the hearing the claimant said nothing about sustaining injuries or having gone for treatment after this XXXXX 2007 beating until the Tribunal Officer asked him directly whether or not he sustained any injuries at that time. He then said he had injuries to face and kidney. The claimant was unable to provide an explanation for the PIF omission about sustaining kidney injuries and about going to the hospital. I draw an adverse credibility finding as a result. I find the medical report9 that was disclosed on the day of the hearing to be suspect. I place no probative value on the medical reports in light of the discrepancies. As previously discussed the claimant's evidence was inconsistent and no explanation was provided.

I also do not accept as plausible that he would tell the police officer details about their intimate behaviour prior to the attack if he was seriously seeking assistance and hoping to make a formal complaint against the attackers. I do not find it credible that in 2007 the same man who stated he hesitated in reporting to police in 2003 would unnecessarily volunteer such information in the circumstances testified to. In the circumstances of this claimant based on his own evidence I find the claimant to be untruthful about his experiences in Kazakhstan prior to coming to Canada.

Many of the disclosed personal documents were obtained shortly before the hearing date despite being told by his lawyer after he arrived here that he should collect supporting documents. In support of his claim that he is homosexual the claimant provided a letter10 dated 9 March 2010 from XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX support group for LGBT refugee claimants. This letter was written for the purpose of confirming the claimant's membership since January 2010. The claimant arrived in Canada on 18 June 2008. The Tribunal Officer asked him why he did not become a member of 519 until a couple months ago and he said he did not know of XXXXX existence until then. I find on a balance of probabilities that it is highly improbable he did not know of the existence of XXXXX XXXXX before this. Within two weeks of arriving in Canada, the claimant attended the Gay Pride Parade in Toronto with a Russian speaking friend. He provided photos11 of himself at the event. I do not on a balance of probabilities accept that XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX would not have come to the claimant's attention at anytime during the Pride Parade. I also do not accept at that time and place that the claimant would not have had the opportunity or the motivation to use the Russian speaking friend to elicit information about the location of the gay community and events in Toronto. The claimant was watching and participating in photo opportunities with parade participants surrounded by gay men both on and off floats who were carrying signs and information about the Toronto Gay Community. This address and resource centre for gays is highly visible and well known in Toronto and would have been advertised at the parade. I find the claimant lacks credibility about why he did not join XXXXX prior to XXXXX 2010. I am not satisfied on a balance of probabilities that the claimant is a member of the particular social group of homosexual men as alleged.

The claimant testified that he has not been in a gay relationship since his arrival in Canada. The claimant testified he had a gay relationship prior to coming to Canada with XXXXX who he met in 2003 when XXXXX was fourteen. The claimant and XXXXX became intimate in XXXXX 2005 just after XXXXX turned sixteen and the claimant was twenty three. The claimant testified he did not know the meaning of 'age of consent' or that in Kazakhstan it is eighteen years of age. At the hearing the claimant testified he and XXXXX began living together in XXXXX 2007 after his aunt left him the key to her apartment. This information was not consistent with the PIF. In the PIF the claimant did not indicate they lived together. He said they used the apartment to spend time together. He said in the PIF XXXXX house and neighbourhood was separate from his. I find the claimant provided inconsistent information about his living arrangements. The claimant also contradicted himself about XXXXX parents' knowledge of their relationship. At the hearing he testified that they knew they were intimate and in the PIF he said he was "certain XXXXX parents did not know the real truth of our relationship and thought of us only as friends". He did not provide a satisfactory explanation for the inconsistencies.

On the day of the hearing the claimant provided a statement from his mother to a notary public made on XXXXX XXXXX 201012 wherein she states he is gay, never dated girls and was in a serious relationship with XXXXX since 2005. The Tribunal Officer asked the claimant if he had asked his mother to prepare the statement and he answered in the affirmative. The claimant testified to telling his mother what to state in the letter including that he was gay and that she knew he was. I give little weight to the letter that was clearly prepared for no other purpose than this hearing.
The claimant provided no documents pre dating XXXXX XXXXX 2010 to support his claim that he and XXXXX remain in contact, explaining they communicate using Skype.
The claimant repeatedly contradicted himself during the hearing and between the oral testimony and the PIF.

In the PIF the claimant stated he heard from others that an acquaintance was murdered in his apartment. The victim was gay and the three men arrested and sentenced to lengthy jail sentences were also gay. The claimant also wrote in the PIF no one could believe the men sentenced could have done this. No news articles or other documents were disclosed concerning this "publicized" murder. I do not know why this incident was included in the PIF. I did not rely on this information as I did not see the relevance. I draw no conclusion from this information in my determination about the claim.

There were so many inconsistencies and contradicted information provided in the evidence in this claim that I did not find sufficient evidence upon which I could find the claimant to be a refugee or person in need of protection. I do not find that the claimant has established himself to be homosexual or to have been targeted in Kazakhstan because he is homosexual or perceived to be homosexual. I find the claimant has failed to discharge his onus of establishing he has a well founded fear of persecution in Kazakhstan. I find there is insufficient persuasive evidence upon which to base a decision that the claimant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

I accept that the claimant is a citizen of Kazakhstan. I do not accept that he has established himself to be homosexual, a person who faces a reasonable chance of persecution or on a balance of probabilities someone who would be subject to risk to life or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if returned to Kazakhstan.
I find the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

After considering the totality of evidence and written submissions I reject the claim.
